title: Heatmap Pass 4 — Combinations

correction_carried_forward.issue: passes 2 and 3 referred to signal_credibility.py as built_b10 in a few places
correction_carried_forward.correction: built_b10 is weighted_consensus_system.py per pass 1. signal_credibility.py was never assigned its own pass-1 asset ID. Treated as an uncatalogued asset in this pass, not built_b10.

candidates.source: Source 1 - externally answered questions never asked
candidates.question: Does a per-market Information Leakage Score, computed on this project's own canonical Geo/Elections population, show excess pre-event price discovery, and does it correlate with the directional-skill harness's cohort?

pass1_assets.adequacy: PARTIAL - 73.1% cross-source agreement, primary-with-fallback; adequate for a first pass, real caveat since ILS timing precision depends on price accuracy

candidates.what_would_make_it_false: ILS computed on this population shows no differential pre-event price movement relative to a matched baseline, or ILS-high markets show no excess concentration of instr_v7-classified skilled traders.
candidates.why_not_closed: Pass-2 D8 group has RQ-ILS-001 as ABANDONED-UNTESTED, never run on any population. Published paper validated ILS on a likely broader/all-category population; this project's Geo/Elections-only canonical population has never been checked. Cross-validating against instr_v7's cohort is a check the source paper had no reason to run.

external_basis.effect_size: skilled accounts + market makers (<3.5% of accounts) capture >30% of platform gains

candidates.cost_floor_problem: Published effect size is a concentration statistic (share of gains captured), not a per-trade edge in price units - cannot be compared to cost floors (geo 0.0005-0.010, elections 0.0056-0.020) without fresh derivation. May turn out smaller once conditioned to this population and netted of fees. NOT assumed to clear.
candidates.placebo_objection_note: Characterization question, not an action-on-positions proposal.

candidates.question: Does adopting the published, Monte-Carlo-validated Signal Credibility Index specification improve on the project's own stalled, annotation-only signal_credibility.py?

pass1_assets.adequacy: live (corrected in pass 1's scripts-fork), annotation-only, never graduated past its internal gate

candidates.what_would_make_it_false: Credibility-weighted signal built on the published spec shows no accuracy improvement, or the paper's own tau*=0.27 threshold fails to transfer.
candidates.why_not_closed: RQ-SCI-001 (pass-2 D4) is ABANDONED-UNTESTED for the validation study - internal gate (>=20 resolved markets) never reached. This candidate adopts an already-externally-validated specification instead of waiting on the internal gate.
candidates.cost_floor_problem: N/A - signal-quality question, not a raw-edge claim.

candidates.source: Source 1 - externally answered questions never asked
candidates.question: Does a Gomez-Cram-style split-half skill classification, applied to this project's own Geo/Elections canonical population, find a comparable skilled minority, and does it overlap with instr_v7's persistence cohort?
candidates.what_would_make_it_false: No comparable skilled-minority fraction in Geo/Elections specifically, or zero overlap with instr_v7's 146-trader cohort.
candidates.why_not_closed: RQ3.2 (pass-2 D3) was CONFOUNDED then ABANDONED-UNTESTED using the project's own two prior framings, neither of which used Gomez-Cram's actual split-half method. Pass-3's jobA_7 answers RQ3.2 for all-Polymarket only, not this project's canonical population, and not cross-validated against instr_v7.
candidates.cost_floor_problem: N/A directly - population-characterization question. Any downstream trading application needs its own cost-floor test.
candidates.placebo_objection_note: Characterizes a population; does not propose acting on it. If a later step proposed trading on the identified minority's positions, it would need to independently clear the same activity-matched-placebo test that killed A8-A11 - noted, not assumed away.

candidates.question: Does re-weighting own_market_calibration.py by position size instead of price reproduce the external paper's rising-with-horizon shape?

pass1_assets.adequacy: PROVEN as instrument for existing weighting; re-weighting reuses the same validated machinery

candidates.what_would_make_it_false: Re-weighted slope still falls with horizon - same shape as today - ruling out weighting as the explanation.
candidates.why_not_closed: Pass 2 has no register entry for own-market calibration at all (live, non-ruled-on finding). Pass 3's jobB_1 only identified weighting as a candidate explanation, explicitly did not test it.

external_basis.note: larger positions are associated with prices further from truth

candidates.cost_floor_problem: N/A - shape/methodology question. Outcome bears on whether the near-resolution slope (~1.29, largest deviation, concentrated at price extremes) is over/under-stated by price-weighting - project already characterized this deviation as cost-floor-scale (~1-2pp).

candidates.question: Did maker-labeled (is_taker=0) trades appear after Polymarket's CLOB v2 maker-rebate program (2026-04-28)?

pass1_assets.adequacy: UNVALIDATED - zero maker rows as of last full audit; this candidate re-checks with a date split

candidates.what_would_make_it_false: is_taker=0 count remains exactly zero after 2026-04-28 too.
candidates.what_true_would_mean: Maker rows appearing only post-2026-04-28 would be strong evidence the pre-date absence was a real market-structure fact, not a permanent detection blindness - and would sharpen jobB_5's diagnosis (relayer-batching hypothesis predicts maker rows should still be zero/misattributed even post-rebate if the true cause is hash-attribution).
candidates.why_not_closed: This exact date-split test appears nowhere in pass 1 or pass 2. is_taker was flagged dead with 'root cause not established'. Pass 3 raises the question but explicitly does not run it.
candidates.cost_floor_problem: N/A - data-integrity/instrument-diagnosis question. If repairable, unlocks a new execution-quality dimension currently unmeasurable.

candidates.question: Does inspecting matched maker/taker transaction hashes show single-hash settlement for both sides (relayer batching), independent of the CLOB v2 rebate program?

pass1_assets.adequacy: PROVEN but 3.57% coverage - the only maker/taker-adjacent ground truth the project holds, thin

candidates.what_would_make_it_false: Matched maker/taker pairs show genuinely distinct transaction hashes per side, ruling out relayer batching.
candidates.why_not_closed: jobB_5 raises this from secondary sources only; pass 3 could not settle it empirically (barred from touching project data). This candidate settles it against the project's own data.
candidates.feasibility_caveat: order_book_snapshots' 3.57% coverage may make this infeasible to test with adequate n - a data-availability floor, a different kind of cost-floor problem.

candidates.question: Would recomputing the presplit-edge cohort/selection rule as of today's data (with instr_v6 post-fix) narrow the CI to exclude zero?

pass1_assets.adequacy: PROVEN as pinned record - must NOT be overwritten
PARTIAL, but deterministic since 2026-09-06 fix - adequate for a NEW measurement, though pre-fix placebos remain non-reconstructable

candidates.what_would_make_it_false: Recomputed CI still includes zero even with a larger effective sample.
candidates.cost_floor_problem: Existing point estimate (+0.0316) already clears geopolitics' range comfortably and sits within elections' upper range - if narrowed to exclude zero, economically meaningful, not merely statistically distinguishable. The one NULL-UNDERPOWERED entry with an effect size already known to clear the floor.
candidates.placebo_objection_note: Design already includes a matched placebo by construction (instr_v6 post-fix) - does not introduce a new naive-selector risk.

candidates.question: N/A - reported as an honest negative, not a live candidate
candidates.reason: Pre-split BH-skilled cohort (146 traders) is capped by definition - defined by trades before a fixed T_split=2026-04-01. Cannot grow by waiting, unlike A1's post-split cohort. Reopening requires either a materially different question (a later/rolling T_split, effectively a new test) or is simply not reachable with the current experimental design.

candidates.question: Would recomputing the persistence cohort's aggregate two-way clustered edge test with positions accumulated since 2026-09-06 narrow the CI to exclude zero?
candidates.reachability: Directionally reachable via accumulation (post-split positions CAN grow with time, unlike A3), magnitude NOT assessed - this pass does not run measurements.
candidates.what_would_make_it_false: CI [-0.0151,0.0362] still includes zero at whatever n_pairs has grown to.
candidates.cost_floor_problem: Not restated here; see A4 in pass 2 for baseline figures.

candidates.reachability: Reachable but requires a build step first - unlike D1, no evidence found it was ever coded. Implementation status should be confirmed before assuming it's merely an execution gap.

candidates.question: Does execution timing (absolute or relative) correlate with directional accuracy or realized edge within instr_v7's validated persistence cohort?
candidates.reachability: Reachable now - instr_v7 exists and is validated (post-dates the original n=4 test).

pass1_assets.adequacy: PROVEN - did not exist in current form when RQ-EXEC-001 was last touched (2026-06-07)

candidates.what_would_make_it_false: No significant relationship (or a reversed one, replicating the n=4 finding of later entry) between timing and accuracy/edge within the cohort.
candidates.why_not_closed: Pass-2's D5 'what would reopen it' just says the deferred validation was never resumed. This candidate is materially re-specified: original test used n=4 external data and predates instr_v7's validated form.
candidates.why_highest_leverage: Project's working theory (Della Vedova-style decomposition, independently supported by jobB_4) holds directional skill doesn't convert into capturable copy-trade edge (A6) or mispricing-marking power (A8-A11). If timing correlates with skill/edge within the validated cohort, that's the first evidence pointing toward WHICH execution dimension might matter, rather than reconfirming naive presence-based signals don't work.

external_basis.note: No new external citation specific to RQ-EXEC-001 from pass 3; draws on D5's own n=4 finding (pass 2) and jobB_4's general Della Vedova support.

candidates.cost_floor_problem: Indirect - within-cohort skill-marker characterization, not itself a raw-edge claim. Any downstream signal needs its own cost-floor test.
candidates.placebo_objection_note: Tests a property (timing) OF an already-validated skilled group - does not propose a new selection criterion tested against a placebo, so partially escapes the A8-A11 objection. BUT if turned into a new presence-based mispricing marker for others to use, that would need to independently clear the same matched-placebo test A8 already ran (and which already found the presence-based version fails at 4/6 horizons). Does NOT inherit validity from instr_v7's classification for that downstream use - objection would need to be re-run, not assumed satisfied.

candidates.rejection_reason: Explicitly retired by design decision (2026-09-05-canonical-skill-metric-design.md SS5): 'flagged, explicitly out of scope - not reused, not repaired.' Reviving would re-collapse distinguishable dimensions into one scalar - the exact mistake the replacement design avoided ('the exact pattern the M6 precedent warned about').

candidates.question: Does Pool C membership churn (entries/exits across the 70 recorded dates) show a stable core population versus a high-turnover fringe, and does that split correlate with instr_v7's classification?

candidates.why_not_closed: Does not require geo_elo's score to be valid - uses only the broader, less-condemned pool-membership filter. Pool C's base-rate confound (A11) is about market-level absence, a different axis. Nothing in pass 2 addresses trader-level membership stability.
candidates.note: This is the task's own example question ('what does a rating time series answer that a cross-section does not'), answered directly: a stability question, independent of rating validity.
Capturability framing moot (A6). Remaining open use (within-cohort skill-marker, not copy-trade mechanism) is exactly S3-8's proposal - not duplicated.
